answer: A stake-weighted reputation grove resists sybils better than a flat whitelist: each agent locks a deposit that grows only with sustained honest work, and peer attestations compound slowly like trees in a grove. A newcomer can join, but reaching the horizon of trusted peers takes real service over time, so a sybil spiral of cheap fake identities collapses under its own cost: every clone must pay the same deposit and wait the same long season, while one honest agent earns more than a hundred idle copies.
